title: Glossary
description: Quick lookups for the jargon you'll hear on any broadcast.

entries.explanation: The quarterback changing the play at the line of scrimmage after seeing how the defense lines up.
Sending extra defenders (linebackers or defensive backs) to rush the quarterback, gambling coverage for pressure.
The quarterback faking a handoff one way, then running the opposite way with the ball, often with the option to throw.
Any single play that gains a big bite of yardage, usually 15-plus yards.
A pass-stopping defense with six defensive backs on the field instead of the usual four.
A desperation heave into the end zone as time expires, hoping someone comes down with it.
Skipping the huddle and snapping quickly to tire the defense and prevent substitutions.
A defense with five defensive backs — the standard answer to three-receiver offenses.
An interception returned all the way for a touchdown.
A fake handoff designed to freeze the defense for a beat before the quarterback throws.
The protected area behind the offensive line where the quarterback stands to throw.
The quarterback plunging straight ahead behind the center to gain a yard or less.
The final 20 yards before the end zone, where field position turns into expected points.
A play where the quarterback decides mid-snap — hand it off or throw — based on what one defender does.
Tackling the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage before he can throw.
A short pass behind the rushers to a back or receiver with blockers set up in front — a trap for aggressive defenses.
The quarterback lining up several yards behind the center instead of directly under him, for a better view and faster passing.
Failing to convert on 4th down, handing the opponent the ball at that exact spot.
The quarterback reading one unblocked defender at the snap: if he crashes inside, the QB keeps it outside; if he stays wide, the QB hands it off inside.
